key_insight: A MicroUS-specific self-supervised foundation model learned from over 1.7 million unlabeled prostate images and improved downstream performance, especially when labeled data were scarce.
clinical_relevance: This could help build more accurate prostate MicroUS tools for segmentation and lesion detection while reducing the amount of expert annotation needed.
method: Pretrained {micro}FM with DINOv2-style self-supervised learning on 1,736,391 unlabeled MicroUS images from 780 patients.
Fine-tuned and tested the model on prostate capsule segmentation, urethra segmentation, and prostate cancer lesion localization.
Compared performance against randomly initialized models and foundation models pretrained on natural, medical, and ultrasound images.
evidence_signal: Across three cohorts, {micro}FM achieved stronger Dice and HD95 results for segmentation and about 0.75 sensitivity at two false positives per 3D volume for lesion localization, with the biggest gains at 10% training scans.
watch_item: The model was pretrained retrospectively at a single institution and did not include explicit 3D modeling, which may limit generalizability.
paper_title: Data-Efficient Prostate Micro-Ultrasound Image Analysis using a Modality-specific Foundation Model
